compatible.executable_observation: flask_cors/core.py has no Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network response-header constant or emission path, so a private-network request cannot be authorized by Flask-CORS.
compatible.subject: Add Tests for Python 3.10, 3.9 (#314)

focal_property: For a CORS request carrying Access-Control-Request-Private-Network: true, Flask-CORS does not emit Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true unless the application explicitly opts in to private-network access.

invalidated.executable_observation: flask_cors/core.py adds the private-network request and response constants and unconditionally emits Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true for a matching request header, without any application opt-in.
invalidated.subject: Adding 'Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network = true' header for new google chrome specification

source.executable_observation: The shared CORS core introduces authorization-sensitive response headers through false-by-default options and emits Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true only when supports_credentials is enabled; no private-network authorization header exists.
source.subject: Version 2.0 Refactor
